subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a short informational passage and asks how the author introduces, illustrates, or develops one key person, event, or idea. Read the passage first, then answer using only what the passage says.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The honeybee may be small, but it is one of the hardest workers in nature. A single honeybee can visit up to a hundred flowers in one trip away from the hive. As it lands on each flower, yellow pollen sticks to the tiny hairs on its body. The bee then carries that pollen to the next flower, helping the plant make seeds. Without this quiet work, many of the fruits and vegetables people eat could not grow.

In the first sentence, how does the author introduce the honeybee?
items.answer: The author introduces the honeybee by stating directly that it is small but one of the hardest workers in nature, which sets up the idea that the rest of the passage will explain.

steps: Find the first sentence: 'The honeybee may be small, but it is one of the hardest workers in nature.'
Notice that this sentence names the subject (the honeybee) and makes a claim about it (it is a hard worker).
This is the introduction because it tells the reader what idea the passage will develop before giving any examples.
So the author introduces the honeybee by stating that it is small but one of nature's hardest workers.
solution.answer: The author introduces the honeybee by stating directly that it is small but one of the hardest workers in nature, which sets up the idea that the rest of the passage will explain.

As the lava cools, it hardens into solid rock and can build up over time into a mountain.

solution.answer: The author introduces the volcano by giving a clear definition, stating that volcanoes are openings in the Earth's surface where hot melted rock can escape.

Recycling helps protect the planet in simple, everyday ways. When people recycle paper, fewer trees need to be cut down to make new paper. Recycling cans and bottles saves energy, because it takes far less power to melt down old metal than to make it from scratch. solution.answer: One example is that recycling paper means fewer trees are cut down (other correct answers: recycling cans and bottles saves energy, or recycling keeps trash out of landfills).

The water cycle is the journey water takes as it moves around our planet. First, heat from the sun warms water in oceans, rivers, and lakes, turning some of it into an invisible gas that rises into the air. High in the sky, this gas cools and forms tiny droplets that gather into clouds. When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall back to the ground as rain or snow. The water then flows back into rivers and oceans, and the cycle begins again.

What is the main job of the first sentence, 'The water cycle is the journey water takes as it moves around our planet'?
items.answer: The first sentence introduces the topic by defining the water cycle as the journey water takes as it moves around the planet, before the later sentences explain each step.

steps: Read the first sentence and notice it explains what the water cycle is.
It gives a general definition rather than a specific step.
The sentences that follow describe the steps of the cycle in order.
So the first sentence's job is to introduce and define the topic for the reader.
solution.answer: The first sentence introduces the topic by defining the water cycle as the journey water takes as it moves around the planet, before the later sentences explain each step.
